source.text: Οὐαὶ δὲ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι κλείετε τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ὑμεῖς γὰρ οὐκ εἰσέρχεσθε, οὐδὲ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἀφίετε εἰσελθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Woe but to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you shut the kingdom of the heavens before the men; you for not enter, nor those entering do you allow to enter.

en.L: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you shut the kingdom of the heavens in front of {{gender:people|men}}; for you yourselves do not enter, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in.
en.B: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You bar the way into the kingdom of heaven so that people cannot get in. You do not go in yourselves, and when others are on their way in, you stop them.
en.R: How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees! You are hypocrites! You keep people from entering the kingdom of heaven. You will not go in yourselves, and you stop others who are trying to go in.

fr.L: Mais malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites ! Car vous fermez le royaume des cieux devant les {{gender:gens|hommes}} ; car vous-mêmes, vous n’entrez pas, et ceux qui entrent, vous ne les laissez pas entrer.
fr.B: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites que vous êtes ! Vous barrez aux gens l’entrée du royaume des cieux. Vous-mêmes n’y entrez pas, et ceux qui sont en train d’y entrer, vous les en empêchez.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous, spécialistes de la Loi et Pharisiens ! Vous êtes des hypocrites ! Vous empêchez les gens d’entrer dans le royaume des cieux. Vous-mêmes, vous n’y entrez pas, et vous arrêtez les autres qui essaient d’entrer.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning over those facing God's judgment
decisions.reason: The prophets used the cry over those who would not turn back (Isaiah 5:8-22). As in 11:21, it is a lament and a warning, not a wish for harm.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who act a part, whose piety is a performance
decisions.reason: The word first meant a stage actor. Jesus has used it of those who practice their religion for an audience (6:2, 5, 16; 15:7).

decisions.choice: no verse 14, following the SBLGNT
alternatives: verse 14 included: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour the houses of widows and make long prayers for show; therefore you will receive greater condemnation", the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts and several early versions lack this verse. Many later manuscripts have it, some before 23:13 and some after, in words that match Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47. Verse numbers were added long after the Gospels were written, so the number 14 is left out. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: shut the kingdom: keep people from entering God's rule by their teaching and example
decisions.reason: The kingdom is pictured as a house with a door. By their teaching the leaders turn people away from Jesus, through whom the kingdom comes (21:31-32).

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you ... You are hypocrites! (R); Woe to you (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 11:21, Readable explains the old word "woe". Every woe in this chapter is worded the same way at each level.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law
decisions.reason: As in 2:4, Readable says what the scribes were.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites (L), hypocrites que vous êtes (B); Quel malheur pour vous, spécialistes de la Loi et Pharisiens ! Vous êtes des hypocrites ! (R)
alternatives: Quel malheur ce sera pour vous (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in Matthew 11:21 and Luke 11:42: "Malheur à" is still understood in French and carries both grief and warning (m1), so Balanced keeps it. Every woe in this chapter is worded the same way at each level, as in English.

source.text: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι περιάγετε τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὴν ξηρὰν ποιῆσαι ἕνα προσήλυτον, καὶ ὅταν γένηται ποιεῖτε αὐτὸν υἱὸν γεέννης διπλότερον ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you go around the sea and the dry [land] to make one proselyte, and when he becomes [one] you make him a son of Gehenna twofold more than you.

en.L: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around sea and dry land to make one proselyte, and when [that] happens, you make {{gender:them|him}} a {{gender:child|son}} of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves.
en.B: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You journey across sea and land to win over one convert. Then, once you have done so, you turn that convert into someone twice as fit for hell as you are.
en.R: How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees! You are hypocrites! You travel over sea and land to get one person to follow your teaching. And when you do, you make that person deserve hell twice as much as you do.

fr.L: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites ! Car vous parcourez la mer et la terre ferme pour faire un seul prosélyte, et quand c’est fait, vous en faites un {{gender:enfant|fils}} de la géhenne deux fois plus que vous.
fr.B: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites que vous êtes ! Vous parcourez la mer et la terre pour gagner un seul converti. Puis, quand vous y êtes parvenus, vous faites de ce converti quelqu’un qui mérite l’enfer deux fois plus que vous.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous, spécialistes de la Loi et Pharisiens ! Vous êtes des hypocrites ! Vous voyagez sur la mer et sur la terre pour amener une seule personne à suivre votre enseignement. Et quand vous y arrivez, vous faites de cette personne quelqu’un qui mérite l’enfer deux fois plus que vous.

decisions.choice: proselyte: a Gentile who turned to the God of Israel and took on the law
alternatives: a Jew who joined the Pharisees
decisions.reason: The word was used of Gentile converts to Judaism. Some think Jesus means people won over to the Pharisees' way of keeping the law, but the word points to Gentiles.

decisions.choice: travel around sea and dry land: go to any length
decisions.reason: Sea and dry land together stand for everywhere.

decisions.choice: a son of Gehenna: one who belongs to Gehenna and is headed for it
alternatives: a child born in the valley of Hinnom
decisions.reason: To be the son of something is to share its nature or belong to it (compare 8:12). Gehenna is the place of final judgment by fire (see 5:22).

decisions.choice: hell (B, R); Gehenna (L)
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, Literal keeps the place name and Balanced and Readable translate it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}} a {{gender:child|son}}
decisions.reason: The convert could be a man or a woman, so the inclusive form is the default. Balanced and Readable say "that convert" and "that person".

decisions.choice: twice as fit for hell (B); deserve hell twice as much (R)
alternatives: a son of hell twice over
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom from the third meaning decision.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you; teachers of the law; You are hypocrites! (R)
alternatives: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in this chapter (see 23:13).

decisions.choice: vous en faites un {{gender:enfant|fils}} (L), one span
alternatives: {{gender:faites de cette personne|faites de lui}} un {{gender:enfant|fils}}
decisions.reason: English Literal needs two spans ("them", "child"). French "en" refers to the convert without marking gender, so only the noun takes the setting.

decisions.choice: la géhenne (L); l’enfer (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in 5:22: Literal keeps the place name, as the English does, and Balanced and Readable say "hell". The same in 23:33.

source.text: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοὶ οἱ λέγοντες· Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ ναῷ, οὐδέν ἐστιν, ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ χρυσῷ τοῦ ναοῦ ὀφείλει.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, guides blind, those saying, Whoever swears by the temple, nothing it is; whoever but swears by the gold of the temple, is bound.

en.L: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound [by the oath].'
en.B: Woe to you, blind guides! This is what you teach: 'Swearing by the temple counts for nothing. But swear by the gold of the temple, and you must keep your oath.'
en.R: How terrible it will be for you! You are like blind people trying to lead others. You say, 'If someone makes a promise and swears by the temple, the promise does not count. But if someone swears by the gold in the temple, that person must keep the promise.'

fr.L: Malheur à vous, guides aveugles, qui dites : “Quiconque jure par le temple, ce n’est rien ; mais quiconque jure par l’or du temple est tenu [par son serment].”
fr.B: Malheur à vous, guides aveugles ! Voici ce que vous enseignez : “Jurer par le temple, cela ne compte pas. Mais si l’on jure par l’or du temple, on doit tenir son serment.”
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous ! Vous êtes comme des aveugles qui essaient de guider les autres. Vous dites : “Si quelqu’un fait une promesse et jure par le temple, sa promesse ne compte pas. Mais si quelqu’un jure par l’or du temple, il doit tenir sa promesse.”

decisions.choice: blind guides: teachers who cannot see the way themselves
decisions.reason: Jesus has called the Pharisees blind guides of the blind (15:14).

decisions.choice: oaths by holy things: swearing by something sacred to guarantee a promise
decisions.reason: People backed their promises by swearing by the temple, the altar or heaven. Some teachers ranked such oaths and held only some of them binding. Jesus has already forbidden oaths altogether (5:33-37).

decisions.choice: the gold of the temple: the gold on the building, or the gold given to it
decisions.reason: Gold covered parts of the temple, and gifts of gold were kept in its treasury. Either way the gold owed its holiness to the temple.

decisions.choice: is bound: owes what was sworn, and must keep the oath
decisions.reason: The verb means to owe. The one who swears is in debt for his oath.

decisions.choice: like blind people trying to lead others; makes a promise and swears
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture and says what an oath was for.

source.text: μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί, τίς γὰρ μείζων ἐστίν, ὁ χρυσὸς ἢ ὁ ναὸς ὁ ἁγιάσας τὸν χρυσόν;

records.literal_gloss: Fools and blind, which for greater is, the gold or the temple the having made holy the gold?

en.L: Fools and blind [men]! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that has made the gold holy?
en.B: Foolish and blind! Which is greater, then: the gold, or the temple that has set the gold apart as holy?
en.R: You are foolish and blind! The temple is what makes the gold holy. So which is more important, the gold or the temple?

fr.L: Insensés et aveugles ! Car lequel est le plus grand, l’or ou le temple qui a rendu l’or saint ?
fr.B: Fous et aveugles ! Qu’est-ce qui est le plus grand, l’or, ou le temple qui a consacré l’or ?
fr.R: Vous êtes fous et aveugles ! C’est le temple qui rend l’or saint. Alors qu’est-ce qui est le plus important, l’or ou le temple ?

decisions.choice: fools: people without sense, who cannot see what is plain
decisions.reason: In 5:22 Jesus forbids calling a brother a fool in anger and contempt. Here he states a judgment on teachers who lead others wrong, as the prophets did (Jeremiah 5:21).

decisions.choice: made holy: set apart for God
decisions.reason: The gold is holy only because it belongs to the temple, God's house.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable states what makes the gold holy, so the question is easy to answer.

source.text: καί· Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, οὐδέν ἐστιν, ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ δώρῳ τῷ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ὀφείλει.

records.literal_gloss: And, Whoever swears by the altar, nothing it is; whoever but swears by the gift the upon it, is bound.

en.L: And [you say], 'Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it is bound [by the oath].'
en.B: You also teach: 'Swearing by the altar counts for nothing. But swear by the gift lying on it, and you must keep your oath.'
en.R: You also say, 'If someone swears by the altar, the promise does not count. But if someone swears by the gift on the altar, that person must keep the promise.'

fr.L: Et [vous dites] : “Quiconque jure par l’autel, ce n’est rien ; mais quiconque jure par l’offrande qui est dessus est tenu [par son serment].”
fr.B: Vous enseignez aussi : “Jurer par l’autel, cela ne compte pas. Mais si l’on jure par l’offrande déposée dessus, on doit tenir son serment.”
fr.R: Vous dites aussi : “Si quelqu’un jure par l’autel, sa promesse ne compte pas. Mais si quelqu’un jure par l’offrande posée sur l’autel, il doit tenir sa promesse.”

decisions.choice: the altar: the altar of burnt offering in the temple court; the gift: the offering laid on it
decisions.reason: Offerings were burned on the great altar that stood before the temple building (5:23-24).

decisions.choice: and: the words "you say" are understood from 23:16
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "and" before the quotation. It adds a second example of the teaching quoted in 23:16.

decisions.choice: [you say] (L); You also teach (B); You also say (R)
decisions.reason: Every level supplies the verb that the Greek leaves understood.

source.text: τυφλοί, τί γὰρ μεῖζον, τὸ δῶρον ἢ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ ἁγιάζον τὸ δῶρον;

records.literal_gloss: Blind, which for greater, the gift or the altar the making holy the gift?

en.L: Blind [ones]! For which [is] greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy?
en.B: How blind you are! Which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sets the gift apart as holy?
en.R: You are blind! The altar is what makes the gift holy. So which is more important, the gift or the altar?

fr.L: Aveugles ! Car lequel est le plus grand, l’offrande ou l’autel qui rend l’offrande sainte ?
fr.B: Que vous êtes aveugles ! Qu’est-ce qui est le plus grand, l’offrande, ou l’autel qui consacre l’offrande ?
fr.R: Vous êtes aveugles ! C’est l’autel qui rend l’offrande sainte. Alors qu’est-ce qui est le plus important, l’offrande ou l’autel ?

decisions.choice: the altar makes the gift holy: Exodus 29:37
decisions.reason: The law says that whatever touches the altar becomes holy. The gift draws its holiness from the altar, not the other way round.

decisions.choice: Blind, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Fools and blind, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "Fools and blind", as in 23:17. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the question
decisions.reason: As in 23:17, Readable states what makes the gift holy before asking the question.

source.text: ὁ οὖν ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] therefore having sworn by the altar swears by it and by all the things upon it;

en.L: So the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything that is on it.
en.B: So whoever swears by the altar is swearing by the altar and by all that lies on it.
en.R: So swearing by the altar means swearing by the altar and by everything on it.

fr.L: Celui donc qui jure par l’autel jure par lui et par tout ce qui est dessus.
fr.B: Ainsi, celui qui jure par l’autel jure par l’autel et par tout ce qui se trouve dessus.
fr.R: Alors, jurer par l’autel, c’est jurer par l’autel et par tout ce qui est dessus.

decisions.choice: therefore: the conclusion of 23:16-19, that every oath by a holy thing binds
decisions.reason: The ranking of oaths falls apart: the greater holds the lesser, so an oath by either is binding.

source.text: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ ναῷ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ κατοικοῦντι αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] having sworn by the temple swears by it and by the [one] dwelling in it;

en.L: And the one who swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it.
en.B: And whoever swears by the temple is swearing by the temple and by the one who dwells there.
en.R: And swearing by the temple means swearing by the temple and by God, who lives there.

fr.L: Et celui qui jure par le temple jure par lui et par celui qui l’habite.
fr.B: Et celui qui jure par le temple jure par le temple et par celui qui y demeure.
fr.R: Et jurer par le temple, c’est jurer par le temple et par Dieu, qui y habite.

decisions.choice: the one who dwells in it: God, whose presence the temple houses
decisions.reason: Solomon built the temple as a house for God to dwell in (1 Kings 8:13; Psalm 135:21). An oath by the temple is an oath by God.

decisions.choice: God
alternatives: the one who dwells in it
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who dwells in the temple.

source.text: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὀμνύει ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] having sworn by the heaven swears by the throne of the God and by the [one] sitting upon it.

en.L: And the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits on it.
en.B: And whoever swears by heaven is swearing by God's throne and by the one seated on it.
en.R: And swearing by heaven means swearing by God's throne and by God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, who sits on it.

fr.L: Et celui qui jure par le ciel jure par le trône de Dieu et par celui qui est assis dessus.
fr.B: Et celui qui jure par le ciel jure par le trône de Dieu et par celui qui y siège.
fr.R: Et jurer par le ciel, c’est jurer par le trône de Dieu et par Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, qui est assis sur ce trône.

decisions.choice: heaven is God's throne: Isaiah 66:1, as in 5:34
decisions.reason: God says, "Heaven is my throne." Every oath, however it is worded, is made before God.

decisions.choice: God himself
alternatives: the one who sits on it
decisions.reason: Readable names the one seated on the throne.

source.text: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ ἄνηθον καὶ τὸ κύμινον, καὶ ἀφήκατε τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου, τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὸ ἔλεος καὶ τὴν πίστιν· ταῦτα ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ ἀφιέναι.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you tithe the mint and the dill and the cumin, and you have neglected the weightier [things] of the law, the justice and the mercy and the faithfulness; these [things] it was necessary to do and those not to neglect.

en.L: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and you have neglected the weightier [matters] of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you ought to have done, and not neglected those.
en.B: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You set aside for God a tenth even of your mint, dill and cumin, yet you have abandoned what weighs most in the law: justice, mercy and faithfulness. These are what you should have done, while still not abandoning the others.
en.R: How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees! You are hypocrites! You give God one tenth of everything, even of the little plants you grow for flavor, like mint, dill and cumin. But you do not obey the most important parts of the law. You do not treat people fairly, you do not show mercy, and you are not faithful. These are the things you should have done. And you should have kept on giving a tenth as well.

fr.L: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites ! Car vous donnez la dîme de la menthe, de l’aneth et du cumin, et vous avez laissé de côté les [points] les plus importants de la Loi : la justice, la miséricorde et la fidélité ; c’est ceci qu’il fallait faire, sans négliger cela.
fr.B: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites que vous êtes ! Vous donnez à Dieu le dixième même de votre menthe, de votre aneth et de votre cumin, mais vous avez abandonné ce qui a le plus de poids dans la Loi : la justice, la miséricorde et la fidélité. C’est cela qu’il fallait pratiquer, sans abandonner pour autant le reste.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous, spécialistes de la Loi et Pharisiens ! Vous êtes des hypocrites ! Vous donnez à Dieu un dixième de tout, même des petites plantes que vous cultivez pour donner du goût, comme la menthe, l’aneth et le cumin. Mais vous n’obéissez pas aux parties les plus importantes de la Loi. Vous ne traitez pas les gens avec justice, vous n’avez pas de pitié, et vous n’êtes pas fidèles. C’est cela que vous auriez dû faire. Et vous auriez dû continuer aussi à donner le dixième.

decisions.choice: tithe: give a tenth to God; mint, dill and cumin: small garden herbs
decisions.reason: The law required a tenth of grain, wine, oil and produce (Leviticus 27:30; Deuteronomy 14:22-23). The Pharisees counted even the smallest herbs used for flavor.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: being true and reliable, toward God and toward others
decisions.reason: The word usually means faith in Matthew (8:10; 9:2). Here it stands in a list with justice and mercy that recalls Micah 6:8 and Hosea 12:7, and most likely means faithfulness, though the two senses overlap.

decisions.choice: justice: fair and right dealing with others
decisions.reason: The word can mean judgment, but here it is the justice the prophets demanded (Micah 6:8; Zechariah 7:9).

decisions.choice: these ... those: the weightier matters first, but tithing still kept
decisions.reason: Jesus does not set tithing aside. He ranks it below justice, mercy and faithfulness, which they have neglected.

decisions.choice: faithfulness (L, B); you are not faithful (R)
decisions.reason: The key term "faith" gives way to "faithfulness" here, as the second meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: set aside for God a tenth (B); give God one tenth; the little plants you grow for flavor; giving a tenth as well (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what tithing was and what "these" and "those" refer to.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you; teachers of the law; You are hypocrites! (R)
alternatives: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in this chapter (see 23:13).

decisions.choice: la fidélité (L, B); vous n’êtes pas fidèles (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, the word usually rendered "la foi" means here being true and reliable toward God and others (m2), which French says with "fidélité".

source.text: ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοί, οἱ διϋλίζοντες τὸν κώνωπα τὴν δὲ κάμηλον καταπίνοντες.

records.literal_gloss: Guides blind, those straining out the gnat, the but camel swallowing.

en.L: Blind guides, who strain out the gnat but swallow the camel!
en.B: Blind guides! You sieve a gnat out of your drink and swallow a camel whole.
en.R: You are like blind people trying to lead others! You pour your drink through a cloth to take out a tiny bug. But then you swallow a whole camel!

fr.L: Guides aveugles, qui filtrez le moucheron et avalez le chameau !
fr.B: Guides aveugles ! Vous passez votre boisson au filtre pour en ôter un moucheron, et vous avalez un chameau tout entier.
fr.R: Vous êtes comme des aveugles qui essaient de guider les autres ! Vous versez votre boisson à travers un tissu pour enlever un tout petit insecte. Mais ensuite, vous avalez un chameau entier !

decisions.choice: straining a gnat, swallowing a camel: great care over tiny matters and none over great ones
decisions.reason: The smallest creature and one of the largest stand for the least and greatest commands (23:23). Both were unclean to eat (Leviticus 11:4, 20-23).

decisions.choice: strain out: pour wine or water through a cloth to remove insects
decisions.reason: Careful Jews strained their drink so as not to swallow an unclean insect.

decisions.choice: out of your drink (B); pour your drink through a cloth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was strained.

source.text: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι καθαρίζετε τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ἐξ ἁρπαγῆς καὶ ἀκρασίας.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, inside but they are full of robbery and self-indulgence.

en.L: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, but inside they are full of robbery and lack of self-control.
en.B: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You wash the outside of cup and plate, but inside they are filled by robbery and self-indulgence.
en.R: How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees! You are hypocrites! You wash the outside of your cups and dishes. But the food and drink inside them come from cheating people and from your own greed.

fr.L: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites ! Car vous purifiez l’extérieur de la coupe et du plat, mais à l’intérieur ils sont pleins de rapine et d’intempérance.
fr.B: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites que vous êtes ! Vous lavez l’extérieur de la coupe et du plat, mais au-dedans, ils sont remplis de ce que vous avez volé et de vos excès.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous, spécialistes de la Loi et Pharisiens ! Vous êtes des hypocrites ! Vous lavez l’extérieur de vos coupes et de vos plats. Mais la nourriture et la boisson qui sont dedans viennent de ce que vous avez pris aux autres en les trompant, et de votre propre avidité.

decisions.choice: cleaning the outside of the cup: ritual washing of vessels
decisions.reason: The Pharisees washed cups and dishes to keep them ritually clean (15:2; Mark 7:4), and debated how the outside and inside of a vessel affected each other.

decisions.choice: full of robbery and self-indulgence: the contents were gained by greed and consumed without restraint
decisions.reason: The Greek says they are full "from" robbery: what fills them comes from taking what belongs to others. The cup stands for the people themselves, clean outside and greedy within (23:26).

decisions.choice: self-indulgence, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: unrighteousness, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "unrighteousness" or other words. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the food and drink inside them come from cheating people and from your own greed
alternatives: they are full of robbery and self-indulgence
decisions.reason: Readable says what fills the cups, from the second meaning decision.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you; teachers of the law; You are hypocrites! (R)
alternatives: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in this chapter (see 23:13).

source.text: Φαρισαῖε τυφλέ, καθάρισον πρῶτον τὸ ἐντὸς τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, ἵνα γένηται καὶ τὸ ἐκτὸς αὐτοῦ καθαρόν.

records.literal_gloss: Pharisee blind, clean first the inside of the cup and of the dish, so that may become also the outside of it clean.

en.L: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and of the dish, so that the outside of it may become clean too.
en.B: Blind Pharisee! Make the inside of cup and plate clean first, so that the outside becomes clean too.
en.R: You blind Pharisee! First make the inside of the cup and the dish clean. Then the outside will be clean too.

fr.L: Pharisien aveugle ! Purifie d’abord l’intérieur de la coupe et du plat, afin que l’extérieur aussi devienne pur.
fr.B: Pharisien aveugle ! Nettoie d’abord l’intérieur de la coupe et du plat, afin que l’extérieur devienne pur lui aussi.
fr.R: Pharisien aveugle ! Rends d’abord propre l’intérieur de la coupe et du plat. Alors l’extérieur sera propre aussi.

decisions.choice: clean the inside first: a clean heart makes the whole person clean
decisions.reason: What is inside makes a person clean or unclean (15:11, 18-20). The cup is a picture of the Pharisee himself.

decisions.choice: Blind Pharisee: one Pharisee addressed as an example of all
decisions.reason: Jesus turns to the singular to speak to each of them in person.

decisions.choice: and of the dish, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the cup only, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "and of the dish", and the following "of it" is singular. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: "tu" to the blind Pharisee
decisions.reason: The Greek turns to one Pharisee in the singular, as an example of all (m2). French shows the change that English "you" hides, so every level says "tu" here and goes back to "vous" in 23:27.

source.text: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι παρομοιάζετε τάφοις κεκονιαμένοις, οἵτινες ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνονται ὡραῖοι ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ὀστέων νεκρῶν καὶ πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας·

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you are like tombs whitewashed, which outwardly indeed appear beautiful, inside but are full of bones of dead and of all uncleanness;

en.L: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which on the outside appear beautiful, but inside are full of the bones of [the] dead and of all uncleanness.
en.B: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You resemble tombs coated with whitewash. From outside they look fine, but within they are full of the bones of the dead and every kind of uncleanness.
en.R: How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees! You are hypocrites! You are like graves that have been painted white. They look beautiful on the outside. But inside they are full of dead people's bones and of everything that makes a person unclean.

fr.L: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites ! Car vous ressemblez à des tombeaux passés à la chaux, qui à l’extérieur paraissent beaux, mais à l’intérieur sont remplis d’os de morts et de toute impureté.
fr.B: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites que vous êtes ! Vous êtes comme des tombeaux passés à la chaux : vus de l’extérieur, ils ont belle apparence, mais au-dedans ils sont pleins d’os de morts et de toutes sortes d’impuretés.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous, spécialistes de la Loi et Pharisiens ! Vous êtes des hypocrites ! Vous êtes comme des tombes peintes en blanc. De l’extérieur, elles sont belles. Mais à l’intérieur, elles sont pleines d’os de gens morts et de tout ce qui rend une personne impure.

decisions.choice: whitewashed tombs: graves marked with white lime
decisions.reason: Touching a grave made a person unclean for seven days (Numbers 19:16). Graves near roads were marked with lime so that travelers, especially pilgrims coming to the festivals, could avoid them.

decisions.choice: uncleanness: the impurity of death, a picture of moral impurity
decisions.reason: A corpse made everything near it unclean. Jesus uses it as a picture of what fills the hypocrites inside (23:28).

decisions.choice: graves
decisions.reason: Readable uses the more common word.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you; teachers of the law; You are hypocrites! (R)
alternatives: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in this chapter (see 23:13).

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνεσθε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δίκαιοι, ἔσωθεν δέ ἐστε μεστοὶ ὑποκρίσεως καὶ ἀνομίας.

records.literal_gloss: Thus also you outwardly indeed appear to the men righteous, inwardly but you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.

en.L: So you also outwardly appear righteous to {{gender:people|men}}, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
en.B: You are the same. To others you look righteous from the outside, but within you are full of hypocrisy and of disregard for God's law.
en.R: You are like that too. On the outside, people think you are righteous and do what God wants. But inside, you are full of pretending, and you do not obey God's law.

fr.L: Ainsi vous aussi, à l’extérieur vous paraissez justes aux {{gender:gens|hommes}}, mais à l’intérieur vous êtes pleins d’hypocrisie et d’iniquité.
fr.B: Vous êtes pareils : de l’extérieur, vous paraissez justes aux yeux des autres, mais au-dedans vous êtes pleins d’hypocrisie et de mépris pour la Loi de Dieu.
fr.R: Vous êtes comme ça, vous aussi. De l’extérieur, les gens pensent que vous êtes justes et que vous faites ce que Dieu veut. Mais à l’intérieur, vous n’êtes que faux-semblants, et vous n’obéissez pas à la Loi de Dieu.

decisions.choice: righteous: doing what God requires
alternatives: having a right standing before God
decisions.reason: As in 5:20, righteousness is a life that does God's will. They look righteous but are not.

decisions.choice: lawlessness: disregard of God's law
decisions.reason: The word means living as if there were no law. Jesus uses it of those who do not do God's will (7:23; 13:41; 24:12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: disregard for God's law (B); pretending; you do not obey God's law (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what lawlessness is. Readable explains hypocrisy as pretending.

decisions.choice: iniquité (L)
decisions.reason: The word means disregard of God's law (m2). "Iniquité" is the established French word for it, and its make-up ("without equity") is close to the Greek "without law"; Balanced and Readable say what it is, as the English does. "Juste" is the term sheet's word for righteous.

source.text: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τοὺς τάφους τῶν προφητῶν καὶ κοσμεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν δικαίων, καὶ λέγετε· Εἰ ἤμεθα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, οὐκ ἂν ἤμεθα αὐτῶν κοινωνοὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι τῶν προφητῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, \v 30 and you say, If we had been in the days of the fathers of us, not we would have been of them partners in the blood of the prophets;

en.L: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, \v 30 and you say, 'If we had been [alive] in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the prophets.'
en.B: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You put up tombs for the prophets and adorn the memorials of the righteous. \v 30 Then you declare, 'If we had been alive when our ancestors were, we would never have joined them in killing the prophets.'
en.R: How terrible it will be for you, teachers of the law and Pharisees! You are hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets. You decorate the graves of righteous people. \v 30 And you say, 'If we had lived back when our ancestors did, we would not have helped them kill the prophets.'

fr.L: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites ! Car vous bâtissez les tombeaux des prophètes et vous ornez les monuments des justes, \v 30 et vous dites : “Si nous avions été [là] aux jours de nos pères, nous n’aurions pas été leurs complices dans le sang des prophètes.”
fr.B: Malheur à vous, scribes et Pharisiens, hypocrites que vous êtes ! Vous élevez des tombeaux pour les prophètes et vous décorez les monuments des justes. \v 30 Puis vous déclarez : “Si nous avions vécu au temps de nos ancêtres, nous ne nous serions jamais joints à eux pour tuer les prophètes.”
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous, spécialistes de la Loi et Pharisiens ! Vous êtes des hypocrites ! Vous construisez des tombeaux pour les prophètes. Vous décorez les tombes des gens justes. \v 30 Et vous dites : “Si nous avions vécu à l’époque de nos ancêtres, nous ne les aurions pas aidés à tuer les prophètes.”

decisions.choice: building and adorning tombs: honoring the prophets and the righteous dead
decisions.reason: In Jesus's time monuments were built over the tombs of prophets and holy people near Jerusalem as a mark of honor.

decisions.choice: partners in the blood of the prophets: sharing in the killing of the prophets
alternatives: related to the prophets by blood
decisions.reason: Blood stands for a killing. Israel had killed prophets in the past (2 Chronicles 24:20-21; Jeremiah 26:20-23).

decisions.choice: our fathers: our ancestors
decisions.reason: The word is used of earlier generations of Israel.

decisions.choice: killing the prophets (B); helped them kill (R)
alternatives: in the blood of the prophets
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the blood means, from the second meaning decision.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you; teachers of the law; You are hypocrites! (R)
alternatives: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in this chapter (see 23:13).

source.text: ὥστε μαρτυρεῖτε ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν φονευσάντων τοὺς προφήτας.

records.literal_gloss: So you testify to yourselves that sons you are of those having murdered the prophets.

en.L: So you testify against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
en.B: Your own words are evidence against you: you are the sons of the prophets' murderers.
en.R: So your own words show that you belong to the family of the people who murdered the prophets.

fr.L: Ainsi vous témoignez contre vous-mêmes que vous êtes fils de ceux qui ont assassiné les prophètes.
fr.B: Vos propres paroles témoignent contre vous : vous êtes les fils des assassins des prophètes.
fr.R: Alors vos propres paroles montrent que vous faites partie de la famille des gens qui ont assassiné les prophètes.

decisions.choice: sons of those who murdered: their descendants, and like them
decisions.reason: They call these people "our fathers" (23:30) and so admit they are their sons. In Scripture a son is often one who shares a father's character, as the next verse implies.

decisions.choice: you testify against yourselves: your own words count against you
alternatives: you testify in your own favor
decisions.reason: The Greek says "to yourselves". In context their claim turns into evidence against them.

decisions.choice: belong to the family of
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom.

source.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς πληρώσατε τὸ μέτρον τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And you fill up the measure of the fathers of you.

en.L: And you, fill up the measure of your fathers!
en.B: Fill up, then, the measure of your ancestors' sins!
en.R: So go ahead and finish the evil things your ancestors started!

fr.L: Et vous, comblez la mesure de vos pères !
fr.B: Allez-y donc, comblez la mesure des péchés de vos ancêtres !
fr.R: Alors allez-y, finissez le mal que vos ancêtres ont commencé !

decisions.choice: fill up the measure: complete the full amount of sin before judgment comes
decisions.reason: Scripture speaks of sin reaching its full measure before God judges (Genesis 15:16; 1 Thessalonians 2:16). Their fathers killed the prophets; they will finish the work by killing Jesus and his messengers (23:34).

decisions.choice: fill up: a command spoken in bitter irony
decisions.reason: Jesus does not want them to sin. The command says that they will surely do it.

decisions.choice: fill up, a command, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: you have filled up; you will fill up, the readings of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a past or future form instead of the command. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: sins (B); the evil things ... started (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the measure is filled with, from the first meaning decision.

source.text: ὄφεις γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς φύγητε ἀπὸ τῆς κρίσεως τῆς γεέννης;

records.literal_gloss: Serpents, offspring of vipers, how may you escape from the sentence of the Gehenna?

en.L: Serpents! Offspring of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of Gehenna?
en.B: You snakes! You family of snakes! How can you flee from the sentence of hell?
en.R: You are snakes! You are like a family of poisonous snakes! There is no way you can escape being judged and sent to hell.

fr.L: Serpents ! Progéniture de vipères ! Comment échapperez-vous au jugement de la géhenne ?
fr.B: Serpents ! Enfants de serpents ! Comment pourriez-vous fuir la condamnation à l’enfer ?
fr.R: Vous êtes des serpents ! Vous êtes comme une famille de serpents venimeux ! Vous ne pourrez pas échapper au jugement de Dieu qui vous enverra en enfer.

decisions.choice: offspring of vipers: the words of John the Baptist (3:7), used by Jesus in 12:34
decisions.reason: Calling people children of snakes describes their nature: dangerous and false. The wording is the same as in 3:7 and 12:34 at each level.

decisions.choice: the sentence of Gehenna: being condemned to Gehenna
alternatives: the judgment that takes place in Gehenna
decisions.reason: The judgment is God's sentence that sends them to Gehenna (5:22, 29-30).

decisions.choice: how will you escape: a question that expects no answer
decisions.reason: The question means that they cannot escape.

decisions.choice: Serpents! Offspring of vipers! (L); You snakes! You family of snakes! (B); You are snakes! You are like a family of poisonous snakes! (R)
decisions.reason: The second phrase keeps the wording of 3:7 and 12:34 at each level; the first word, snakes, is added before it.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects.

decisions.choice: hell (B, R); Gehenna (L)
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, Literal keeps the place name and Balanced and Readable translate it.

decisions.choice: Progéniture de vipères (L); Enfants de serpents (B); une famille de serpents venimeux (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 12:34 in French at each level, as the English keeps 3:7 and 12:34; the first word, "Serpents", is added before it.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω πρὸς ὑμᾶς προφήτας καὶ σοφοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς· ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενεῖτε καὶ σταυρώσετε, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μαστιγώσετε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν καὶ διώξετε ἀπὸ πόλεως εἰς πόλιν·

records.literal_gloss: Because of this, behold, I send to you prophets and wise [men] and scribes; of them you will kill and crucify, and of them you will flog in the synagogues of you and persecute from town to town;

en.L: Because of this, look, I am sending you prophets and wise [ones] and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town,
en.B: That is why I am sending you prophets, sages and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; others you will whip in your synagogues and hound from town to town.
en.R: That is why I am sending you prophets, wise teachers, and teachers of the law. You will kill some of them. You will even nail some of them to crosses. You will beat others with whips in your synagogues. You will chase them from one town to the next.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, voici, moi j’envoie vers vous des prophètes, des sages et des scribes ; vous en tuerez et [en] crucifierez, et vous en fouetterez dans vos synagogues et [en] poursuivrez de ville en ville,
fr.B: C’est pourquoi je vous envoie des prophètes, des sages et des scribes. Vous tuerez et crucifierez les uns ; vous fouetterez les autres dans vos synagogues et vous les pourchasserez de ville en ville.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que je vous envoie des prophètes, des enseignants sages et des spécialistes de la Loi. Vous tuerez certains d’entre eux. Vous en clouerez même sur des croix. Vous frapperez les autres à coups de fouet dans vos synagogues. Vous les poursuivrez d’une ville à l’autre.

decisions.choice: I am sending: Jesus speaks as the one who sends God's messengers
decisions.reason: In Luke 11:49 the same saying is given as the words of "the Wisdom of God". In Matthew Jesus himself sends the messengers, as God sent the prophets of old (2 Chronicles 36:15-16).

decisions.choice: prophets, wise ones and scribes: the messengers Jesus will send, his own followers
alternatives: the prophets of the Old Testament
decisions.reason: Jesus has spoken of his disciples as prophets (5:12; 10:41) and of a scribe trained for the kingdom (13:52). He has warned them they will be flogged in synagogues and persecuted from town to town (10:17, 23).

decisions.choice: crucify: the Roman form of execution; flog: the beating given by synagogue courts
decisions.reason: Only Rome crucified, so the leaders would kill by handing over to Roman power, as with Jesus (20:19). Synagogue courts could sentence a person to a beating of up to forty lashes (Deuteronomy 25:3).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: sages (B); wise teachers (R)
decisions.reason: "Wise men" might recall the visitors of 2:1, who are called by another word. Balanced and Readable choose words that do not.

decisions.choice: ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into 23:35. Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence there.

decisions.choice: vous en tuerez ... vous en fouetterez (L)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 11:49: the French partitive "en" says "some of them" just as the Greek "of them" does, so Literal needs no bracketed "some".

source.text: ὅπως ἔλθῃ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς πᾶν αἷμα δίκαιον ἐκχυννόμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος Ἅβελ τοῦ δικαίου ἕως τοῦ αἵματος Ζαχαρίου υἱοῦ Βαραχίου, ὃν ἐφονεύσατε μεταξὺ τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.

records.literal_gloss: so that may come upon you all blood righteous being poured out on the earth from the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.

en.L: so that upon you may come all the righteous blood poured out on the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.
en.B: And so the guilt for all the innocent blood poured out on the earth will fall on you, from the blood of Abel, a righteous man, to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.
en.R: So you will be punished for the murder of every innocent person whose blood has been spilled on the earth. That goes from the murder of Abel, who did what was right, to the murder of Zechariah son of Barachiah. You killed him between the temple building and the altar.

fr.L: afin que vienne sur vous tout le sang juste répandu sur la terre, depuis le sang d’Abel le juste jusqu’au sang de Zacharie, fils de Barachie, que vous avez assassiné entre le temple et l’autel.
fr.B: Ainsi la culpabilité pour tout le sang innocent répandu sur la terre retombera sur vous, depuis le sang d’Abel, un homme juste, jusqu’au sang de Zacharie, fils de Barachie, que vous avez assassiné entre le temple et l’autel.
fr.R: Ainsi, vous serez punis pour le meurtre de toutes les personnes innocentes dont le sang a coulé sur la terre. Cela va du meurtre d’Abel, qui faisait ce qui est juste, jusqu’au meurtre de Zacharie, fils de Barachie. Vous l’avez tué entre le bâtiment du temple et l’autel.

decisions.choice: Abel the righteous: the first murder, Genesis 4:8-10
decisions.reason: Cain killed his brother Abel, and Abel's blood cried out to God from the ground. Abel is called righteous in Hebrews 11:4.

decisions.choice: Zechariah son of Barachiah: most likely the priest Zechariah of 2 Chronicles 24:20-22
alternatives: the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah (Zechariah 1:1)
Zechariah son of Baris, killed in the temple in the war with Rome
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 24:20-22 tells of Zechariah, killed in the court of the temple and asking God to avenge it. Chronicles comes last in the Hebrew Bible, so Abel to Zechariah spans the whole of Scripture. But that Zechariah is called the son of Jehoiada; the prophet Zechariah was the son of Berechiah, and no killing of him is recorded. Luke 11:51 has no father's name. How to explain the name is uncertain.

decisions.choice: son of Barachiah, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words lacking, as in at least one early manuscript
decisions.reason: At least one early manuscript lacks "son of Barachiah", perhaps because of the difficulty with 2 Chronicles 24. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: upon you: this generation shares the guilt of all who killed God's messengers
alternatives: only the people who killed Zechariah
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks as if the present generation had done the killings, because they are about to do the same (23:31-32). The righteous blood is the blood of innocent people.

decisions.choice: innocent blood (B); every innocent person (R)
decisions.reason: Applied to blood, the word means the blood of people who did no wrong.

decisions.choice: the guilt for ... will fall on you (B); you will be punished for the murder of (R)
alternatives: all the righteous blood may come upon you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means for blood to come upon someone: the guilt and punishment for it.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἥξει ταῦτα πάντα ἐπὶ τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, will come these things all upon the generation this.

en.L: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
en.B: Truly I tell you, all these things will fall upon this generation.
en.R: I tell you the truth, the people living now will be punished for all these things.

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis, toutes ces choses viendront sur cette génération.
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis : tout cela retombera sur cette génération.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : les gens qui vivent aujourd’hui seront punis pour tout cela.

decisions.choice: this generation: the people living in Jesus's time
alternatives: the Jewish people in every age
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the phrase of his own contemporaries (11:16; 12:39-45; 24:34).

decisions.choice: all these things: the judgment for the blood of 23:35
decisions.reason: Jesus goes on to foretell the destruction of the temple (24:2), which came in AD 70.

decisions.choice: I tell you the truth
decisions.reason: Readable's settled wording for this formula.

decisions.choice: will be punished for
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for these things to come upon them.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms for the "amen" saying, as in Mark 12:43 and Matthew 5:26.

source.text: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου, ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις ἐπισυνάγει τὰ νοσσία αὐτῆς ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε;

records.literal_gloss: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the [one] killing the prophets and stoning those having been sent to her, how often I wanted to gather together the children of you, the way a hen gathers together the chicks of her under the wings, and not you were willing?

en.L: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her, how often I wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen gathers her chicks under [her] wings, and you were not willing?
en.B: Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You murder the prophets and stone the messengers sent to you. How many times I have wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen draws her chicks under her wings! But you refused.
en.R: Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets. You throw stones at the messengers God sends to you. Many times I wanted to gather your people together and protect them, the way a hen tucks her chicks under her wings. But you would not let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Jérusalem, Jérusalem, [toi] qui tues les prophètes et lapides ceux qui lui sont envoyés, combien de fois j’ai voulu rassembler tes enfants, comme une poule rassemble ses poussins sous les ailes, et vous n’avez pas voulu ?
fr.B: Jérusalem, Jérusalem ! Tu assassines les prophètes et tu lapides les messagers qui te sont envoyés. Que de fois j’ai voulu rassembler tes enfants, comme une poule attire ses poussins sous ses ailes ! Mais vous avez refusé.
fr.R: Jérusalem, Jérusalem ! Tu tues les prophètes. Tu jettes des pierres aux messagers que Dieu t’envoie. Bien souvent, j’ai voulu rassembler tes habitants pour les protéger, comme une poule met ses poussins à l’abri sous ses ailes. Mais vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas laissé faire.

decisions.choice: your children: the people of Jerusalem
alternatives: only the children of the city
decisions.reason: A city's people were called its children.

decisions.choice: a hen gathering her chicks under her wings: God's care and protection for his people
decisions.reason: The Scriptures picture God sheltering his people under his wings (Deuteronomy 32:11; Ruth 2:12; Psalm 91:4).

decisions.choice: how often I wanted: Jesus speaks of a longing for Jerusalem that goes beyond his own visits
alternatives: only the days Jesus spent in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Matthew tells of one visit to Jerusalem. Jesus speaks the way God speaks of sending his messengers again and again (2 Chronicles 36:15-16).

decisions.choice: stoning those sent to her: putting God's messengers to death
alternatives: throwing stones to drive them away
decisions.reason: The priest Zechariah was stoned in the temple court (2 Chronicles 24:20-21; see 23:35).

decisions.choice: those who are sent to her
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks to the city and then of it in the same sentence. Literal keeps that change; Balanced and Readable say "you" throughout.

decisions.choice: an exclamation and a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the sentence as a question that expects no answer. Balanced and Readable state what it means.

decisions.choice: God sends; your people; and protect them; you would not let me
alternatives: those sent; your children; you were not willing
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the sender, explains the idiom, and says what the city refused.

decisions.choice: "tu" to the city, "vous" for the refusal
decisions.reason: As in Luke 13:34: the Greek speaks to Jerusalem in the singular and then says "you were not willing" in the plural, meaning its people. French can show the change that English "you" hides, so every level keeps it.

source.text: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν ἔρημος.

records.literal_gloss: Behold, is left to you the house of you desolate.

en.L: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
en.B: Now your house is being abandoned to you, a desolate place.
en.R: Now your house will be left to you, empty and deserted.

fr.L: Voici, votre maison vous est laissée déserte.
fr.B: Désormais, votre maison va vous être abandonnée, livrée à la désolation.
fr.R: Maintenant, votre maison va vous être laissée, vide et abandonnée.

decisions.choice: your house: the temple, or the city and its people
decisions.reason: The house may be the temple, God's house, which Jesus leaves in 24:1 and whose ruin he foretells in 24:2. Or it may be Jerusalem itself as the home of its people. Either way, God is leaving it without his presence and protection.

decisions.choice: left desolate: abandoned by God, as the prophets warned
decisions.reason: God warned that his house would become a desolation (Jeremiah 22:5; 12:7; 1 Kings 9:7-8).

decisions.choice: desolate, included in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the word lacking, as in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "desolate", and Luke 13:35 has the saying without it. Most manuscripts have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); now (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: empty and deserted
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words.

source.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, οὐ μή με ἴδητε ἀπ’ ἄρτι ἕως ἂν εἴπητε· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: I say for to you, not not me you will see from now until you say, Blessed the [one] coming in name of Lord.

en.L: For I tell you, you will by no means see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from now on until you say, 'Blessed [is] the one who comes in [the] name of [the] Lord.'"
en.B: For I tell you, from now on you will not see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} again until you say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
en.R: I tell you, you will not see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} again until you say, 'May God bless the one who comes in the name of the Lord!'"

fr.L: Car je vous le dis, vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} verrez plus, dès maintenant, jusqu’à ce que vous disiez : “Béni [soit] celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur !” »
fr.B: Car je vous le dis : désormais, vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} verrez plus jusqu’à ce que vous disiez : “Béni soit celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur !” »
fr.R: Je vous le dis : vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reverrez pas avant de dire : “Que Dieu bénisse celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur !” »

decisions.choice: Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord: Psalm 118:26
decisions.reason: The psalm was sung by pilgrims coming to the temple at the festivals. Where the Greek has "Lord", the Hebrew of the psalm has the divine name, YHWH. The crowds used these words when Jesus rode into Jerusalem (21:9).

decisions.choice: until you say: the day of his coming, when Jerusalem will acknowledge him
alternatives: only his entry into the city in 21:9
a welcome that will never come
decisions.reason: Jesus has already entered the city (21:9), so he most likely means his coming in glory (24:30; 26:64). Whether the words will then be a joyful welcome or the acknowledgment of those under judgment is not said.

decisions.choice: by no means see me: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for emphasis.

decisions.choice: the wording of 21:9 at each level
decisions.reason: The psalm is worded as when the crowds sang it at 21:9, so the reader hears the same welcome.

decisions.choice: May God bless
decisions.reason: This word for blessed is a prayer that God will bless, not the word of the Beatitudes. Readable makes the prayer clear.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: In a New Testament quotation the Greek has "Lord", so every level writes "Lord"; the first meaning decision notes the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the French wording of 21:9 at each level
decisions.reason: As in English, the psalm is worded as when the crowds sang it at 21:9: "Béni [soit]" (L), "Béni soit" (B), "Que Dieu bénisse" (R).
